lead.title: Raspberry Pi 5 16GB tops $385, more than triple its launch price
lead.summary: Raspberry Pi raised the 16GB Pi 5 by $80 to $385 (from a $120 January 2025 launch price) and the 16GB Compute Module 5 by $40, with CEO Eben Upton blaming a lack of alternative supply for 16GB DRAM as memory makers prioritize AI data centers. The 8GB Pi 5 lists at $175, so the extra 8GB now costs $210; Raspberry Pi says the increases are temporary and reversible.

top_stories.title: Nous Research releases Arete-27B, a post-trained Qwen3.8-27B open-weight model
top_stories.summary: Post-trained on ~53M tokens against an 803-prompt, seven-category value evaluation; the team reports the propaganda rate dropped from 22% to 1% with no significant performance tradeoffs, with eval dataset, weights and training data public on Hugging Face.

top_stories.title: Unsloth Dynamic v3.1 quants cut tokens ~50% and beat prior quants on accuracy for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
top_stories.summary: Dynamic v3.1 GGUFs match full-precision thinking/token behavior, reporting up to 50% fewer tokens, ~7% faster and ~15% higher accuracy versus same-size quants; the ~9 GB UD-IQ2_XS matches GSQ-RCO IQ3_S scores.

top_stories.title: GeForce RTX 5080 street price nears $2,000, double its $999 MSRP
top_stories.summary: The 16GB Blackwell card trades at roughly two to three times launch MSRP amid the memory-driven supply squeeze; a used RTX 3090 (24GB) or Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32GB) remain the value comparison for local rigs.

top_stories.title: n8n 2.47.0 beta adds an Apps module and agent version/publication history
top_stories.summary: The beta builds, previews and publishes apps from the UI with the n8n Assistant integrated; node-level changes include custom SSL certs for Postgres, webhook signature verification on Mailchimp/Venafi triggers, and OAuth2 as the Zendesk default.

items.title: Ripple-65B-Preview released by ricursiveAI
items.summary: New 65B preview checkpoint uploaded within the last day, climbing the trending list shortly after release.

items.title: kniv v7.1: six open encoders improved without a training run
items.summary: All six kniv open encoders gain on coreference (LitBank) and entity typing via direct weight/ONNX-graph edits: no retraining, INT8 coreference within 0.1 of fp32, 7-16% faster end to end.

items.title: Ammu-1.0 fact-check need classifiers benchmarked at FP16/FP8
items.summary: GPU benchmark of the 17M-150M sequence classifiers keeps 100% of FP32 Macro-F1 in FP16 and 99.8%+ in native FP8, up to 1,813 q/s on a single L4, with the Nano shrinking to 16 MB.

items.title: Four tiny logistic models predict scenes from a backpack's sensors
items.summary: Umwelt-trek ships four open CC BY 4.0 logistic-regression models trained on one minute-by-minute laptop sensor log (GPS, RF sweep, audio band levels), with leave-one-day-out scoring and honest per-card calibration verdicts.

items.title: Ru-Jev v1.3: open 307M typed-decision CPU encoder for Russian
items.summary: MIT-licensed pointwise cross-encoder on mmBERT-base (110M outside embeddings); label-wording augmentation gains on unfamiliar words, with exact McNemar statistics and per-row files released.

items.title: Maple: sub-2-BPW MoE pruning runs Gemma 4 26B at 45 TPS on a 6GB GPU
items.summary: Open-source pruning compresses Mixture-of-Experts LLMs below 2 bits per weight so a 26B Gemma 4 model fits and runs fast on a 6GB GPU — useful for squeezing bigger models into low-end local hardware.

items.title: Reges Code: free AI code editor running entirely on local models
items.summary: A code editor whose AI features run on local models rather than a cloud API, demonstrated alongside Reges Town, a 3D browser world of AI citizens.

items.title: OpenViking: shareable context layer for agent teams
items.summary: Open-source context layer from the Volcengine team lets multiple AI agents share working context, targeting multi-agent setups on local stacks.

items.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark ARM/Blackwell unified-memory PCs gain ground as local AI appliances
items.summary: RTX Spark machines (~NT$150,000-200,000) are drawing labs and studios for on-device inference, with TrendForce expecting roughly 200,000 units in 2026 and up to 1 million in 2027; NVIDIA's Pair feature routes jobs across DGX Spark, RTX Spark, GeForce RTX PCs and Macs.

items.title: ASUS XG Core: 75W USB4 eGPU dock with Radeon RX 9060 XT LP 16GB
items.summary: Formally announced pairing of an RX 9060 XT LP (16GB GDDR6, RDNA 4) with a 75W 40Gbps USB4 design for handhelds and small desktops, citing up to 406 INT4 TOPS; no price or retail date yet.
